newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end at new year low on oversupply fears. [corrected 08:48 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end at new year low on oversupply fears. [corrected 08:48 gmt]

text.p: Stocks closed at this year's lowest level on Monday in weak trading as jitters over share oversupply and a bribery scandal involving the head of a leading commercial bank dampened market sentiment, brokers said.
The composite stock index shed 2.05 percent, or 14.99 points, to a provisional close of 716.45. It was the lowest level so far this year.
The previous closing low was 729.53 on November 11.
Brokers said today's closing level was the lowest since October 9, 1993, when the index closed at 712.35.

"The government's plan to sell 360 billion won worth of Korea Telecom shares this week and list the state-run company next year was to blame," said Lee Kil-woo of Hyundai Securities. (Corrects from "360 million" to "360 billion won")
The finance ministry said last week Korea Telecom would be listed on the Seoul stock market in the first half of 1997.
The Korea Stock Exchange expanded the daily trading band for share price movements on Monday to eight percent up and down from the opening price, from the previous six percent.
Bank shares fell as the weekend arrest of the head of a leading South Korean bank pressured already weak counters, brokers said.
The banking sub-index fell 2.44 percent to 419.81.

On Saturday, state prosecutors said they had arrested Sohn Hong-gyun, president of SEOULBANK, on bribery charges. SEOULBANK is South Korea's sixth largest bank in terms of deposits, and its shares fell 150 won to 4,450 won in active trading.
Brokers said sentiment would remain depressed on Tuesday in the absence of any boosting measure from the government.
Falling customer deposits with securities houses were also to blame for the current depression, analysts said.
The deposits were now estimated at 2.48 trillion won, compared with this year's high of 3.3 trillion won in May.
An overhang of loans for margin trading, estimated at 2.8 trillion won, also weighed on the market.
The market was closed on Saturday due to a computer upgrade. "Introduction of the new system slowed today's trading," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
